newsitem.title: UK: Buba comments prop dlr/mark but 1.50 fails to hold.
newsitem.headline: Buba comments prop dlr/mark but 1.50 fails to hold.

text.p: The dollar was keeping to narrow ranges below 1.50 marks in late European trade after comments from senior Bundesbank officials propelled it briefly above this level in earlier trade.
Currency analysts said with a full schedule of Bundesbank officials speaking over the next three days, these comments could be the start of a fresh round of verbal dollar support.
"Clearly what we're seeing is the Bundesbank go into a strategy of verbal support for the dollar," said James McKay, international economist at PaineWebber in London.

"I don't necessarily think 1.50 is a key level. But it does pose a risk to German economic recovery, particularly since the economic recovery is sensitive to the export sector," said PaineWebber's McKay.

Bundesbank council member Edgar Meister said today the current dollar/mark rate below 1.50 marks was not appropriate, echoing earlier comments from fellow council member Hans-Juergen Krupp that a firmer dollar might seem more appropriate.
Market focus was now on Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer speaking later today at 1700 GMT for further dollar positive comments.

The stronger dollar theme will also be eyed from other Bundesbank members this week. Council member Franz-Christoph Zeitler speaks Wednesday, Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher speaks Thursday and Guntram Palm and chief economist Otmar Issing on Friday.
After today's remarks, the dollar made a brief foray above 1.50 marks to a session high of 1.5007. By 1616 GMT, it settled back to 1.4990/95, still above 1.4970/77 late Monday.
"The Buba comments have helped but there are heavy offers just above 1.50 and good bids at 1.4970 so we're still in fairly tight ranges," said a Swiss bank dealer.
Some analysts see the possibility of the Bundesbank trimming the repo rate if its pro-dollar rhetoric fails.

"There will come a point when the mark's strength will prompt another rate cut," said Julian Jessop, chief European economist at Nikko Europe. "But this would be the early part of next year, certainly not this year."

Although the 1.50 mark level featured in today's Bundesbank comments, currency analysts say dollar/mark would have to slip to the 1.40-1.45 marks area, levels not seen since early this year, before the central bank will be prompted to take action with rates.

The dollar showed little reaction to a U.S. Treasury Department announcement that Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin did not discuss forex with Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka in a phone call today about financial services.

The market has been eyeing keenly official U.S. comment on the dollar after last week's remarks by Japanese finance ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara that the dollar's correction on the yen from 1995 lows was about to end.
Trade was also wary ahead of Wednesday's U.S. producer price data for October. An average of forecasts point to a 0.2-percent increase for the month and a 2.8-percent rise year-on-year.

The OECD's annual review of the U.S. economy released today said full employment and fairly low inflation are likely to continue for the next two years but suggested the Federal Reserve consider a rate rise as insurance against the reemergence of inflation.
The report comes one day before the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Wednesday, but few analysts see any action by the Federal Reserve on interest rates.
